notes: The experiment manipulates fertilizer and seed-predator access to explain reproductive output. It is biologically rich but does not estimate repeated selection on one declared floral trait coordinate.

source_basis: Willmer et al. 2009 Functional Ecology DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2435.2009.01632.x
notes: Floral/pollen VOCs repel ants while beneficial bee visitors are not repelled, but the source does not place those responses on a common plant reproductive-fitness estimand.
Pollination limitation and high fruit predation jointly constrain reproduction across stands/years, but no single plant trait coordinate is the repeated selection estimand.
Restoration context changes bird visitation, bud herbivory and reproduction. The causal coordinate is habitat structure/site context, not one multifunctional plant trait.

Early herbivory changes later antagonists, pollinator visitation and reproduction; reproduction was not pollen limited. The manipulated coordinate is herbivore damage state rather than a registered floral trait axis.
